title: DecisionEvidence v1.0.0
$comment: PINNED AND IMMUTABLE. This file is the authority an offline auditor validates a sealed DecisionEvidence record against, and it stops being editable the moment the first record is sealed under evidence_schema_version 1.0.0. After that point every byte here is load-bearing: a record's seal is a SHA-256 over its canonical bytes, and 'which shape was this record written in' is answerable only by reading the file that carried this exact version string. Changing a description is harmless; changing a constraint retroactively reclassifies records that were valid when written, which is indistinguishable from rewriting history. CHANGES GO IN A NEW FILE: bump the semver, add schema/decision_evidence/vX.Y.Z.json, leave this one alone. This mirrors the discipline already applied to circuits/wealth_suitability/vkey/ - the verification key is committed and CI-pinned specifically so an examiner can check a proof without trusting Memtara's build pipeline, and a schema an examiner cannot re-derive two years later is worth no more than a vkey they cannot. The $id above is an identifier, not a fetch target: an offline auditor validates against their copy of this file as shipped in the verification bundle, and no step of verification may require a network call.

evidence_schema_version.$comment: Inside the object, therefore inside the bytes the seal digests. Not sidecar metadata: an examiner opening this record in 2028 must be able to name the schema it was written under without asking a live registry, and must be able to detect an edit to that claim via the seal.

model.$comment: null here is a signed assertion that no AI system participated in this decision. It is NOT 'we did not record the model'. That second case is expressed as a present object whose leaves are state:unpopulated. The key is mandatory in both cases - a record that omits it is invalid, not permissive.

provenancedBase.$comment: A leaf value plus the provenance of its presence or absence. Always exactly three keys, in every state, so that a record's key set never depends on how much the producing deployment happened to know. state is not derivable from value: 'unpopulated' and 'not_applicable' both carry a null value, and the difference between an admission of ignorance and a signed assertion of non-applicability is the entire point.

decisionAction.$comment: Required wherever it appears. Three variants and no fourth: there is no 'pending', because an evidence record is written about a decision that was reached. A rejection carries this field exactly as an approval does - that symmetry is what keeps the canonical bytes, and therefore the seal, comparable across outcomes.

decisionOutcome.$comment: 'negative' means a verdict was produced and it was negative. 'no_verdict' means no verdict was produced at all - the control could not run. Collapsing the two would let an outage read as a decline. This distinction already exists in backend/api/src/wealth/evidence.rs:180-187 and is promoted here into the schema so that it cannot be lost in a later refactor.

org_type.$comment: Deliberately an open string, not an enum. An evidence reader must not fail closed on an org type added after this schema was pinned; an unrecognised institution type is a thing to report, not a reason to refuse to parse a sealed record.

status.$comment: The decision's own disposition. NOT disclosure_requests.status, which is pipeline state (pending/fulfilled/expired).

input_context_fingerprint.$comment: Sibling of model rather than a child of it. When model is null the decision still had inputs; a fingerprint that vanished along with the AI would leave a non-AI decision with nothing committing to what it was decided on.

assessed_at.$comment: Nullable because a decision can be opened and never assessed - NOT because it was rejected. A rejection has an assessed_at exactly as an approval does. The key is present either way.

decision_logic_version.$comment: Which revision of the rules turned inputs into a verdict. Distinct from policy_version: the policy text can be unchanged while the code and circuit enforcing it are rebuilt.

values.$comment: Integers, strings, booleans and null only. Floats are excluded on purpose: CPython's json.dumps renders 1e300 as 1e+300 and Rust's ryu renders it as 1e300, so a float in the canonical bytes produces a digest that only one of the two verifiers of a sealed pack can reproduce. Encode money in minor units.

disclosed_attributes.$comment: Empty for the wealth flow, and empty by design rather than by omission: the server never held the client's income, liquidity, risk tolerance or holdings. An examiner will look for those figures, so the record says structurally why they are not there.

consent_version.$comment: The consent POLICY version this grant was made under.

purpose_hash.$comment: vault/src/session.rs SessionPolicy.purpose_hash - the only consent-adjacent value that exists in the system today. It is a purpose binding, not a consent record: no grant time, no subject acknowledgement, no revocation path. Kept as its own field so that populating it can never be mistaken for having obtained consent.

prompt_version.$comment: Which revision of the prompt. Separate from system_prompt_or_policy_id, which says which prompt.

timestamp.$comment: When the model was called. Distinct from decision.timestamps.assessed_at, which times the proof workflow.

performed.$comment: Whether a human review step occurred at all - the human analogue of model:null. Without it, a decision with no review step would have to carry an action that reads as a human verdict, which would be a false statement inside the signed bytes.

override_reason.$comment: Genuinely nullable by meaning: there is no reason when there was no override. Null, never absent.

allOf.$comment: An override with no stated reason is not evidence of anything. This is the one place the schema is stricter than the Rust type, which can only enforce it at the constructor.

uri.$comment: Relative to the verification bundle root, e.g. proof/wealth_suitability.proof. Not an http URL: a bundle that resolves its own contents over the network is not offline-verifiable.

cryptographic_proofs.$comment: Every attempt, accepted and rejected. A pack showing only the accepted proof hides the four that failed first, which is exactly the pattern a reviewer is looking for.

accepted_by_bb_verify.$comment: Whether bb verify exited 0. NOT the decision: a valid proof of unsuitability verifies successfully. The verdict is decision.final_decision.outcome, read from the circuit's public output.
